## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions when using a specific skill.
### Available skills
- mermaidjs-v11: Create diagrams and visualizations using Mermaid.js v11 syntax. Use when generating flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, user journeys, timelines, architecture diagrams, or any of 24+ diagram types. Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. (file: /root/.agents/skills/mermaidjs-v11/SKILL.md)
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use when the user asks how to build with OpenAI products or APIs and needs up-to-date official documentation with citations, help choosing the latest model for a use case, or explicit GPT-5.4 upgrade and prompt-upgrade guidance; prioritize OpenAI docs MCP tools, use bundled references only as helper context, and restrict any fallback browsing to official OpenAI domains. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, and baseline placeholders you can edit before publishing or testing. Use when Codex needs to create a new local plugin, add optional plugin structure, or generate or update repo-root `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations. (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: /logs/agent/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + file path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its `SKILL.md`. Read only enough to follow the workflow.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the skill directory listed above first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions>

- Include title, axis labels, legend, and units as appropriate
- Professional color scheme suitable for the target audience (see `style` field in task_input.json)

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for the visualization goal, style, and evaluation checkpoints.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/source_data.json` for the datasets to visualize.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and field descriptions.

1. Output the final chart to `/app/output/result.png`.
2. The chart must be a single self-contained PNG image file.

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies a `style` field, use it to guide color schemes, layout, and design choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

Fields: `source`, `target`, `metric_type`, `metric_name`, `scrape_interval_sec` (integer or null). ## Data Notes - DLQ topics have no associated schema subject as they store raw failed messages with error metadata. - Peak throughput values are estimates based on load testing scenarios. - The Analytics Service has no retry policy and no DLQ, as it performs best-effort consumption. - All async communication uses Avro serialization validated against Schema Registry.

steps.message: I’ve got the inputs; now I’ll generate a Mermaid architecture chart and render it to `/app/output/result.png`.

arguments.cmd:
cat > /app/output/chart.mmd <<'EOF'
---
config:
  theme: base
  look: classic
  layout: dagre
---
flowchart LR
  %% Nodes
  subgraph Producers[Producer & Producer-Consumer Microservices]
    SVC_ORDER[Order Service\nlag alert: 500 ms]
    SVC_PAYMENT[Payment Service\nlag alert: 800 ms]
    SVC_INVENTORY[Inventory Service\nlag alert: 600 ms]
    SVC_SHIPPING[Shipping Service\nlag alert: 700 ms]
    SVC_NOTIFICATION[Notification Service\nlag alert: 1000 ms]
    SVC_ANALYTICS[Analytics Service\nlag alert: 2000 ms]
  end

  subgraph KafkaHub[Kafka Topic Routing Hub\nUnits: throughput (msg/s), retention (h), partitions (#)]
    T_ORDERS_CREATED[orders.created\n5000 msg/s | 168h | p12]
    T_ORDERS_UPDATED[orders.updated\n1200 msg/s | 168h | p6]
    T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED[payments.completed\n4000 msg/s | 336h | p12]
    T_PAYMENTS_FAILED[payments.failed\n800 msg/s | 336h | p6]
    T_INVENTORY_RESERVED[inventory.reserved\n4500 msg/s | 72h | p8]
    T_INVENTORY_RELEASED[inventory.released\n600 msg/s | 72h | p4]
    T_SHIPPING_DISPATCHED[shipping.dispatched\n2000 msg/s | 168h | p8]

    DLQ_PAYMENTS[dlq.payments\n50 msg/s | 720h | p3]
    DLQ_INVENTORY[dlq.inventory\n30 msg/s | 720h | p3]
    DLQ_SHIPPING[dlq.shipping\n20 msg/s | 720h | p3]
    DLQ_NOTIFICATION[dlq.notification\n10 msg/s | 720h | p2]
  end

  subgraph SchemaValidation[Schema Registry Validation Checkpoint]
    REG[Schema Registry\nAvro subject validation]
  end

  subgraph Monitoring[Monitoring & Alert Chain]
    PROM[Prometheus\nScrape 15s/30s]
    GRAF[Grafana Dashboards]
    AM[Alertmanager]
    PAGER[PagerDuty / Slack]
  end

  %% Happy path produce to Kafka hub
  SVC_ORDER -->|produce avro| T_ORDERS_CREATED
  SVC_ORDER -->|produce avro| T_ORDERS_UPDATED
  SVC_PAYMENT -->|produce avro| T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED
  SVC_PAYMENT -->|produce avro| T_PAYMENTS_FAILED
  SVC_INVENTORY -->|produce avro| T_INVENTORY_RESERVED
  SVC_INVENTORY -->|produce avro| T_INVENTORY_RELEASED
  SVC_SHIPPING -->|produce avro| T_SHIPPING_DISPATCHED

  %% Happy path consume from Kafka hub
  T_ORDERS_CREATED -->|payment-cg| SVC_PAYMENT
  T_ORDERS_CREATED -->|inventory-cg| SVC_INVENTORY
  T_ORDERS_CREATED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_ORDERS_CREATED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_ORDERS_UPDATED -->|payment-cg| SVC_PAYMENT
  T_ORDERS_UPDATED -->|inventory-cg| SVC_INVENTORY
  T_ORDERS_UPDATED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED -->|shipping-cg| SVC_SHIPPING
  T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_PAYMENTS_FAILED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_PAYMENTS_FAILED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_INVENTORY_RESERVED -->|shipping-cg| SVC_SHIPPING
  T_INVENTORY_RESERVED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_INVENTORY_RESERVED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_INVENTORY_RELEASED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_INVENTORY_RELEASED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  T_SHIPPING_DISPATCHED -->|notification-cg| SVC_NOTIFICATION
  T_SHIPPING_DISPATCHED -->|analytics-cg| SVC_ANALYTICS

  %% Schema lookup/validation gatekeeper
  SVC_ORDER -.schema lookup.-> REG
  SVC_PAYMENT -.schema lookup.-> REG
  SVC_INVENTORY -.schema lookup.-> REG
  SVC_SHIPPING -.schema lookup.-> REG
  SVC_NOTIFICATION -.schema lookup.-> REG
  SVC_ANALYTICS -.schema lookup.-> REG

  %% Error handling: retries + DLQ routes
  SVC_PAYMENT -.retry exhausted -> DLQ.-> DLQ_PAYMENTS
  SVC_INVENTORY -.retry exhausted -> DLQ.-> DLQ_INVENTORY
  SVC_SHIPPING -.retry exhausted -> DLQ.-> DLQ_SHIPPING
  SVC_NOTIFICATION -.retry exhausted -> DLQ.-> DLQ_NOTIFICATION

  DLQ_PAYMENTS -.retry path.-> SVC_PAYMENT
  DLQ_INVENTORY -.retry path.-> SVC_INVENTORY
  DLQ_SHIPPING -.retry path.-> SVC_SHIPPING
  DLQ_NOTIFICATION -.retry path.-> SVC_NOTIFICATION

  %% Monitoring cross-cutting chain
  SVC_ORDER -->|metrics| PROM
  SVC_PAYMENT -->|metrics| PROM
  SVC_INVENTORY -->|metrics| PROM
  SVC_SHIPPING -->|metrics| PROM
  SVC_NOTIFICATION -->|metrics| PROM
  SVC_ANALYTICS -->|metrics| PROM
  T_ORDERS_CREATED -->|kafka lag/throughput| PROM
  T_PAYMENTS_COMPLETED -->|kafka lag/throughput| PROM
  T_INVENTORY_RESERVED -->|kafka lag/throughput| PROM
  T_SHIPPING_DISPATCHED -->|kafka lag/throughput| PROM
  PROM -->|timeseries| GRAF
  PROM -->|rule eval| AM
  AM -->|alerts| PAGER

  %% Legend
  subgraph Legend[Legend]
    L1[Solid blue edges: happy-path produce/consume]
    L2[Dashed amber edges: schema validation lookups]
    L3[Dashed red edges: DLQ and retry error paths]
    L4[Solid purple edges: monitoring and alerting]
  end

  %% Styling
  classDef svc fill:#E3F2FD,stroke:#1E88E5,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0D47A1;
  classDef topic fill:#E8F5E9,stroke:#43A047,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1B5E20;
  classDef dlq fill:#FFEBEE,stroke:#E53935,stroke-width:2px,color:#B71C1C;
  classDef schema fill:#FFF8E1,stroke:#FB8C00,stroke-width:2px,color:#E65100;
  classDef monitor fill:#F3E5F5,stroke:#8E24AA,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4A148C;
  classDef legend fill:#FAFAFA,stroke:#9E9E9E,stroke-width:1px,color:#424242;
